messages:
incident-bot: Pager — unusual auth pattern detected: 7,200 failed auth attempts + 120 successful metadata GETs to s3://redwood-logs-staging from 52.86.12.34 over 8m. Possible mirrored credentials. AlertID: INC-2026-4447
alex: seeing the same in grafana — spike started at ~17:03 UTC. Noting a cluster of accesses to /metadata and /tokens endpoints. I'll grab logs.
samantha: @sec-oncall please?
sec-oncall: oncall here. Initial triage: botted auth failures then a handful of valid calls using svc-staging-readonly key. Assume compromised key. What’s customer impact? any exfil?
yves: from quick grep, 18 unique user IDs accessed, no obvious PII in responses but metadata blobs contain path to s3 artifacts. Potential exposure of object paths.
alex: I’m isolating the service account: running
```
# disable service account token
kubectl -n staging patch secret svc-staging-token -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"disabled":"true"}}}'
```
alex: started rotation for svc-staging-readonly in KMS; will create new key and update IAM bindings.
samantha: please snapshot logs and preserve them (retention change) — legal asked to hold everything.
legal-bot: Logging hold requested by @samantha — retention extended to 90d for bucket redwood-incident-1749991230-logs. DO NOT DELETE.
sec-oncall: good. Also spin a honeypot bucket to collect further attempts. @yves can you stand up a fake credentials sink with decoy objects? :eyes: 
yves: on it. Creating bucket redwood-honeypot-1749991230 and adding fake index.json. Will ship access logs to internal S3 and alert on any GET.
alex: I found PUT attempts to customer-artifacts/; three successes from same IP to a path that looks randomized. Blocking IP at edge WAF now.
samantha: phone bridge opened: zoom.us/j/999999999 @sre @sec-oncall @legal-bot
sre: applying WAF block now: waf rule id 67321 set block for 52.86.12.34
sec-oncall: run a query to see which customers had artifacts touched and start customer impact triage. Prioritize customers with regulated data.
yves: Query run — two tenants show write events: tenant-orm and tenant-gamma. Both in staging, not prod. No prod customers touched.
alex: confirm — only staging bucket names. No prod org IDs found. Good.
samantha: still proceed with rotation and full forensic — we treat as credential compromise.
sec-oncall: action list: (1) rotate svc-staging-readonly creds (in progress), (2) revoke tokens and reissue, (3) block IPs (done), (4) preserve logs (done), (5) honeypot (done), (6) legal notified (done), (7) customer notice not required (staging-only) — agree?
legal-bot: Legal acknowledges. No external notice required at this time; keep logs for 6 months. Notify if scope widens.
alex: rotation complete, IAM bindings updated, new key rolled, old key scheduled for deletion in 24h after verifying no breaks.
sec-oncall: ok. Close loop: update incident ticket and set postmortem owner. Assign to @alex for mitigation notes and @yves for forensic artifacts. I'll own key rotation report.
samantha: thanks team. small follow-ups: add a rule to prevent svc tokens being usable from public IPs and add anomaly alert on metadata access patterns.
yves: adding anomaly alert now with threshold 50 metadata GETs/min per key.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-4447 created. Severity: sev2. Paging channel: #incidents. Next update in 30m or on new findings. :white_check_mark:
